quickSummary: Lysosomes contain >50 acid hydrolases active at acidic pH (4.5–5.0) maintained by a membrane V-type H+-ATPase proton pump. They exhibit polymorphism: primary lysosomes, secondary heterophagosomes, residual bodies, and autophagosomes (autophagy). Vacuoles occupy up to 90% of plant cell volume, bounded by a selectively permeable Tonoplast that pumps ions against concentration gradients. Classes include sap, contractile (osmoregulatory in Amoeba), and food vacuoles.

conceptBreakdown.content:
Single membrane-bound spherical digestive vesicles produced by packaging at the trans-Golgi network.

### Acid Hydrolases & pH Maintenance
• **Enzyme Profile**: Contains over 50 hydrolytic digestive enzymes (proteases, nucleases, glycosidases, lipases, phosphatases, sulfatases) active exclusively at an **acidic pH ($\approx 4.5\text{--}5.0$)**.
• **V-type $H^+$-ATPase Pump**: Luminal acidity is actively sustained by a vacuolar-type proton pump in the lysosomal membrane that hydrolyzes ATP to pump $H^+$ ions into the lumen.
• **Safety Mechanism**: If a lysosome accidentally ruptures into the cytosol, the neutral cytosolic pH (~7.2) renders the acid hydrolases inactive, preventing catastrophic self-digestion.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 4.4 Vacuoles & The Tonoplast
conceptBreakdown.title: 4.4 Vacuoles & The Tonoplast
conceptBreakdown.content:
Vacuoles are single-membrane-bound cytoplasmic compartments predominant in mature plant cells (occupying up to 90% of total cellular volume).

### The Tonoplast Membrane
The specialized selectively permeable single vacuolar membrane. Features primary and secondary active transporters that pump ions ($\text{Na}^+, \text{K}^+, \text{Ca}^{2+}, \text{H}^+$) and organic acids against steep concentration gradients into the vacuolar lumen, maintaining internal hypertonicity and cellular turgor.

### Functional Classes
1. **Sap Vacuole**: Stores water, mineral ions, metabolic wastes, and water-soluble **anthocyanin / anthoxanthin** pigments (imparting red, purple, and blue flower petal colors).
2. **Contractile Vacuole**: Present in freshwater protists (*Amoeba, Paramecium*); periodically fills with water and contracts to pump excess water out across the plasma membrane (**Osmoregulation**).
3. **Food Vacuole**: Formed by phagocytic engulfment of nutrients in protists and phagocytic animal cells.
